sections.h2: Who handles property tax inside the Todd County courthouse?
sections.html:
Todd County puts its tax work in one building: the courthouse at 202 East Washington Street in Elkton. All three offices answer through the county switchboard at (270) 265-9966, each on its own extension.

  • Sheriff, ext. 208: takes payment of property tax bills. The sheriff's website lets owners view their bills online and says payment cannot be made there, so ask the office which payment methods it accepts.
  • Property Valuation Administration (PVA), ext. 504: the county's answer for the value of a property and for disputing that value.
  • County clerk, ext. 501: registers vehicles and, after April 15, runs the delinquent-tax process.

The City of Elkton keeps a separate property tax payment link on its own website. If your address is inside the city, ask the city whether a city bill exists in addition to the county bill.

sections.h2: What sets Todd County apart from the counties around it?
sections.html:
Todd County spans 377 square miles and almost none of it is water, 2.6 square miles in all. The legislature created it on April 1, 1820, from parts of Christian and Logan counties, after residents petitioned for a seat of government closer than the two existing ones. It was named for Colonel John Todd, killed at the Battle of Blue Licks in 1782.

Historically the county divides into a northern high country of steep sandstone slopes with oak, walnut and poplar, and a southern low country of rolling limestone flatlands. The lowlands, with Pembroke soil, are known for strong crop yields, and farming is a long-standing local tradition. In the early 1800s a stagecoach hub at what is now Guthrie sent routes out to larger cities. Elkton took its name from the elk that watered at a spring near the center of town, and its courthouse square was laid out as a trapezoid rather than a square, so buildings on both sides catch sunlight longer.

Early settlers came while the area still belonged to Virginia, which set aside southern Kentucky land for Revolutionary War veterans, and the Cherokee had hunted these lands long before. The cities are Elkton, Guthrie and Trenton, with Allensville and Fairview (mostly in Christian County) as census-designated places. Muhlenberg, Logan and Christian counties border Todd, as do Robertson and Montgomery counties in Tennessee. Todd County runs on Central time and has a single public school district, the Todd County School District, with Todd County Central High School.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures say about Todd County homes?
sections.html:
Todd County is estimated at 12,972 residents in July 2025, a 5.9 percent rise since 2020, after a small slide during the 2010s. The housing figures matter most to a seller:

  • The middle of the market is a $166,700 owner-occupied home, the lowest value among the four counties.
  • Owners occupy 76.0 percent of homes, spread across 4,559 households.
  • Typical gross rent is $851, above Taylor and Trigg.
  • 5,313 housing units stood in the county in 2025, and 40 building permits were issued.
  • Household income sits at $61,103, and the trip to work averages 27.8 minutes.

In 2020, 10.8 percent of housing units were vacant and 30.0 percent of occupied homes were rented. Retail sales for 2022 came to $150.3 million. Todd also has the youngest population of the four, with 27.2 percent of residents under 18 and 7.6 percent under 5. About 82.4 percent of adults finished high school, 16.5 percent hold a four-year degree, and 13.9 percent of people under 65 have no health insurance.

sections.h2: How has Todd County's population moved over time?
sections.html:
The headcount peaked around the start of the twentieth century and has hovered near 12,000 for decades. The county has not grown steadily the way Spencer has.

Employment tells a quieter story. Todd County had 208 employer establishments in 2023 with 1,794 jobs, 3.4 percent more than the year before, and a total payroll of $84.5 million. Another 1,118 businesses had no employees at all.

sections.h2: When do Todd County property tax bills go delinquent?
sections.html:
The sheriff's file closes at the end of the day on April 15. Whatever is unpaid moves to the clerk's office, where a recorded lien attaches and the bill is renamed a certificate of delinquency. Until then the state schedule sets the price: 2 percent off if you pay by November 1, the bare amount through year end, a 5 percent surcharge in January and 10 percent afterward, with the sheriff's add-on fee on top.

Once the bill reaches the clerk, monthly interest of one percent runs, and commissions for the clerk and the county attorney follow. In the Revenue Department's sample, a $1,000 bill arrives at the clerk as $1,254, costs $1,387.79 to settle within five business days, and costs a third-party purchaser $1,704.21 at the sale. Waiting adds money fast, and the attorney's commission is waived only during that first five-day window.

sections.h2: When does the Todd County tax sale happen?
sections.html:
Under KRS 134.128 the sale falls 90 to 135 days after the sheriff hands bills to the clerk, a window the Department of Revenue puts at July 14 to August 28 on a regular schedule. Each year the clerk lists the sequence in order: a half-page notice, the published list, the deadline for outside buyers to register, and the sale itself, which begins at 9 AM.

A buyer of up to three bills registers with the county, while anyone wanting more than three registers with the state. The clerk's page points out that a buyer of a bill gets a lien, not the house. Afterward the owner settles with that buyer, who may pile on costs. The county attorney mails notices to owners beforehand, and the list runs in the newspaper roughly a month before the sale.

sections.h2: How do I dispute a Todd County assessment?
sections.html:
The county FAQ sends valuation questions to the PVA in the courthouse, extension 504. A conference there is mandatory. File the appeal at the clerk's office on the workday after the May viewing period ends. A panel of area owners then holds hearings a few weeks later.

The panel wants evidence: nearby sales, an appraisal, construction costs or insurance records. An owner who skips the local step or the hearing cannot continue to the Kentucky Claims Commission. Paid representatives must be professionals such as attorneys, accountants, brokers or appraisers and must hold written authorization.

sections.h2: What does the homestead exemption mean for a Todd County sale?
sections.html:
For 2025 and 2026 the state lets an owner past 65, or totally disabled, subtract $49,100 from the assessed value of a home they live in. The Todd County PVA takes applications through December 31. The benefit stays with the owner, so a buyer files again.

Before closing, get the sheriff's payoff and ask the clerk about older certificates. Delinquent tax is the personal debt of the January 1 owner, and its lien can last eleven years, so a title agent will want a clean record before releasing funds.

faqs.q: Where is a Todd County property tax bill paid?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's office inside the courthouse at 202 East Washington Street, extension 208 of (270) 265-9966. The sheriff's website lets you view bills, and the office can tell you which payment methods it takes.

faqs.q: Who reviews a Todd County assessment I disagree with?
faqs.a: The PVA, at extension 504. Ask for a conference first, because the local board hears only owners who have had one.

faqs.q: What is the Todd County homestead deduction?
faqs.a: The amount is $49,100 through the 2026 tax period, available to owners past 65 or totally disabled. Applications go to the PVA before the year ends.

faqs.q: Can an investor buy my delinquent Todd County bill?
faqs.a: Yes. After April 15 the bill sits at the clerk's office, and an outside purchaser can buy it at the yearly sale and then collect from you.

faqs.q: Can a Todd County house with unpaid tax be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance comes out of the sale price. Get written payoffs from the sheriff and clerk so the buyer's closing agent sees no surprises.
